title: Machine-learning screening reveals enhanced formate selectivity of Cu–Ga for CO₂ electroreduction
summary: A machine-learning high-throughput screen of 465 binary metallic catalysts predicted previously unreported Cu–Ga selectivity for formate production in CO₂ electroreduction. Electrochemical tests of electrodeposited Cu–Ga measured a maximum formate Faradaic efficiency of about 38.4% at −1.05 V_RHE, roughly four times that on bare Cu under the reported conditions. This is a catalyst selectivity result for the tested electrode and electrolyte, not evidence of industrial-scale performance.
ai_technology: DSTAR active-motif machine-learning models with a CO₂-reduction selectivity map
organization: Sogang University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

evidence.tested: A machine-learning high-throughput screen of 465 binary metallic catalysts predicted previously unreported Cu–Ga selectivity for formate production in CO₂ electroreduction.
evidence.unknown: The reported ~38.4% Faradaic efficiency is for the tested electrodeposited Cu–Ga electrode at −1.05 V_RHE in the authors’ cell and electrolyte, and the comparison is to bare Cu under those conditions. The paper discusses other predicted alloy outcomes too; this entry counts the single Cu–Ga study/result once. No device-scale or long-duration performance is established.
evidence.ai_role: The authors combined ML binding-energy predictions with a reaction-selectivity map to screen 465 binary metallic combinations and prioritize Cu–Ga and Cu–Pd behavior for follow-up. Experimental Cu–Ga measurements validated the previously unreported formate-selectivity prediction; the AI-enabled screening supplied the non-obvious target and selectivity hypothesis.
